questionText: What are the main HTTP methods and what is each used for?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can explain the standard meaning of the methods commonly used by REST APIs, choose a method from the requested effect instead of treating every method as a CRUD label, and recognize TRACE and CONNECT as specialized protocol methods.
inScope: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, and OPTIONS as the methods commonly used around REST APIs
TRACE and CONNECT as specialized protocol methods
The target resource and the meaning carried by the method
outOfScope: A claim that POST only means create
A claim that DELETE guarantees physical erasure from storage

claims.statement: The request method is the primary source of HTTP request semantics and indicates the purpose for which the client made the request.

GET transfers a selected representation; HEAD has GET semantics without response content and may omit fields determined only while generating that content; OPTIONS describes communication options; TRACE performs a diagnostic message loop-back; CONNECT establishes a tunnel through a proxy.
POST performs resource-specific processing, PUT creates or replaces target state with the enclosed representation, and DELETE removes the target URI's current association with its functionality.
PATCH requests that the changes described by a patch document be applied to the target resource; the patch media type defines the document's change semantics.
GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE are safe; those safe methods together with PUT and DELETE are idempotent, while POST, PATCH, and CONNECT have no general idempotency guarantee.
DELETE expresses removal of the target resource's URI association and does not prescribe that every stored representation or implementation record be physically destroyed.

examples.title: GET, POST, and DELETE requests for one order API

validation.command: Review each request line, required Host field, JSON media type, and body against RFC 9110 semantics
validation.expected: Each HTTP request is structurally traceable and its method matches the effect explained below it

visuals.title: Core purpose, safety, and idempotency of common REST methods and specialized HTTP methods

notes: RFC 9110 sections 9.1, 9.2, 9.3, and its method registry are the authority for method semantics; RFC 5789 is the authority for PATCH.
The order example teaches request meaning and deliberately does not imply a database implementation.

review.notes: All protocol claims were checked against RFC 9110 and RFC 5789. The prose was independently written in beginner-friendly language.
